title: 2026-10-22_BlackTech_PLEAD_Backdoor_Investigation_839
description: Investigate and respond to a BlackTech PLEAD backdoor incident.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity potentially related to the BlackTech threat group. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: While monitoring network traffic, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host (192.168.50.5) to an unknown destination. Investigate this activity and identify the service responsible for these connections.
levels.solution: Check running services and their network connections. The service name is stored in /tmp/flag1.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their network connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use netstat or ss to list all active connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run 'netstat -tulnp' or 'ss -tulnp' to see the processes using network connections.

levels.title: Analyze Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Now that you've identified the suspicious service, determine how it maintains persistence on the system. Investigate the system's startup configuration to find how this service is automatically started.
levels.solution: Check systemd service configurations and timers. The persistence identifier is stored in /tmp/flag2.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check systemd service configurations and timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run 'systemctl list-timers --all' to list all systemd timers.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Examine the target host for evidence of lateral movement. Determine if the suspicious service is transferring data to other hosts in the network.
levels.solution: Check for scheduled tasks and file transfer activities. The service name is stored in /tmp/flag3.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check for scheduled tasks and file transfer activities.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for cron jobs and systemd services that might transfer files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run 'crontab -l' and 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to check for scheduled tasks.
